title: Perfect descent refining a fixed cartesian model
statement: Let $I$ be a small filtered category, $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a diagram of Noetherian rings, and $c$ a colimiting cocone with point $A$. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be of finite presentation [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Fix $i\in I$, $f_i:X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ of finite presentation, and a cartesian comparison $g:X\to X_i$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(c_i)$ [def-pc-base-change]. Assume the derived categories of modules on all schemes and their open slice sites exist in the fixed derived-category universe [def-pc-derived-category]. If $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], there exist a morphism $a:i\to j$ in $I$, a finitely presented $f_j:X_j\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_j)$, maps $p:X_j\to X_i$, $g_j:X\to X_j$, with cartesian squares over $\operatorname{Spec}(R(a))$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(c_j)$ respectively, $g_j\mathbin{\gg}p=g$, and a perfect $E_j\in D(\mathcal O_{X_j})$ with $Lg_j^*E_j\cong E$ [def-pc-derived-pullback].

proof.text: Restrict to the filtered under-category of i, then a final directed poset by Mathlib IsFiltered.exists_directed (0032). Final functors preserve the colimit of R. Base change Xi to one object of this nonempty poset. Pullback pasting gives an isomorphism between X and the canonical limit pullback.

Transport E by derived pullback along the inverse scheme isomorphism. Derived pullback preserves perfectness. Apply perfect_complex_descends to the directed ring system and the transported perfect object.

Return the resulting stage to I; its object in Under i supplies a:i -> j. Take Xj to be the iterated pullback of the fixed model and p the composite first projection. The cocone equations and universal property construct gj with gj >> p = g. Pullback pasting gives both cartesian squares, and base change preserves all three finite-presentation properties.

Projection equations and pullback extensionality identify gj with the initial pullback isomorphism followed by the canonical base-change map. Compose the descended-object isomorphism with derived pullback composition and identity to obtain Lgj* Ej isomorphic to the original E.

lean.statement:
theorem filtered_cartesian_perfect_descent
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ i : I, IsNoetherianRing (R.obj i)]
    (c : Cocone R) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec c.pt)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}), HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (U : Z.Opens), HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (i : I) (Xi : Scheme.{u}) (fi : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation fi] [QuasiCompact fi] [QuasiSeparated fi]
    (g : X ⟶ Xi) (hcart : IsPullback g f fi (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)))
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : X.IsPerfect E) :
    ∃ (j : I) (a : i ⟶ j) (Xj : Scheme.{u}) (fj : Xj ⟶ Spec (R.obj j)),
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation fj ∧ QuasiCompact fj ∧ QuasiSeparated fj ∧
      ∃ (_hfj : LocallyOfFiniteType fj) (p : Xj ⟶ Xi) (gj : X ⟶ Xj),
        IsPullback p fj fi (Spec.map (R.map a)) ∧ gj ≫ p = g ∧
        IsPullback gj f fj (Spec.map (c.ι.app j)) ∧
        ∃ Ej : schemeDerivedCategory Xj, Xj.IsPerfect Ej ∧
          Nonempty ((derivedPullback gj).obj Ej ≅ E)
